title: Merry and Bobo's Tiny Wishes
markdown:
As the sun began to whisper its goodnight, and the sky turned soft shades of purple and rose, little Merry the meerkat wiggled her curious nose. Merry had bright round eyes. She loved to look at all the nice things in the world. And right beside her, all warm and fluffy, sat Bobo the teddy. Bobo wore a smile made of soft thread. His heart was soft and warm, like a fluffy cloud.

“Oh, Bobo,” squeaked Merry. Her little paws patted the rug with a soft sound. “The stars are getting ready to blink their sleepy eyes. It’s almost time for our tiny wishes.”

Bobo understood Merry’s quietest squeaks. He gave a gentle silent nod. He liked tiny wishes. They felt perfectly, wonderfully just right for a sleepy cozy night.

The rug was a little far from the stars, so they padded softly, like quiet snowflakes, to the big window. The moon, a sliver of creamy light, was peeking over the sleepy hills. And the very first little stars, like tiny diamond dust, were starting to sprinkle across the dark soft sky.

“My first tiny wish,” whispered Merry. Her breath was a soft puff towards the window. “I wish for everyone, everywhere, to feel warm and safe and wonderfully snug in their beds tonight.” Her wish floated out, light as a dandelion seed on a gentle breeze, to find all the sleepy heads.

Bobo gently nudged Merry with his soft nose. His wish was for sweet peaceful dreams for all the little sleepyheads. He imagined a warm soft blanket of quiet slumber, washing over everyone.

Then Merry thought of something else. One wish did not feel quite finished, so she made a second. “I wish that we, you and I, always have the coziest, warmest snuggles together.” She wiggled her tiny toes. A warm flutter of happiness filled her.

Bobo’s little stitched smile grew a tiny bit wider. He wished for more gentle quiet moments, just like this one, sharing the peaceful hush of the evening with his dearest Merry.

And for their very last tiny wish, as more stars began to twinkle like friendly eyes, Merry and Bobo looked at each other. “My third tiny wish,” Merry whispered. Her voice was now so soft, it was like a petal falling. “I wish that tomorrow will be just as lovely and full of gentle fun as today has been.”

Bobo simply snuggled a little closer. It was his quiet way of saying, Mine too, Merry. Mine too. Their little mission of wishing was complete. The window sill was peaceful. The sky was a tapestry of winking stars. The world outside was settling down for a long quiet sleep.

After their important wishing was done, Merry and Bobo padded softly back to their warm and cozy nest. They snuggled down. Merry tucked her twitchy nose under Bobo’s soft ear. Bobo felt perfectly, wonderfully just right beside her. The gentle moonlight painted soft patterns on the wall. The quiet peaceful sounds of the night lulled them. Soon their little eyes grew heavy. They drifted off to sleep, dreaming the sweetest, tiniest dreams under the twinkling stars. And in their little nest, everything was just right.
